questions.question: Find the work done (in kJ) if a force of 750 N pushes a cart of mass 30 kg by 16 m.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• Work is said to be done by a force when the body is displaced actually through some distance in the direction of the applied force.
 
• Since the body is being displaced in the direction of F, therefore work done by the force in displacing the body through a distance s is given by

W = vec F · vec s

Or, W = Fs cos θ

 
• Thus work done by a force is equal to the scalar or dot product of the force and the displacement of the body.

**CALCULATION**__:

Given that:

*⇒ *Force, F = 750 N

*⇒ *displacement, s = 16 m

*⇒ *Work done, w = Fs Cos θ 

Here θ is zero degree so Cos θ = 1

*⇒ W* = 750 × 16

*⇒ W* = 12000 J

To convert Joule into Kilo Joule divide by 1000

*⇒ *w = 12000 / 1000

*⇒ ***Work done, W = 12 KJ**

*⇒ ****__Note:__***** **1 Joule = 0.001 Kilo Joule

The astronaut weighs 90 kgf on Earth. This means that the astronaut weighs 90 x 10 = 900 N (since under Earth's gravity 1kgf = 1N 10 m/s²).

 

On the moon, the acceleration due to gravity is 1/6 of that on Earth, so the astronaut's weight will be 1/6 of his weight on Earth.

 

This gives us 1/6 × 900 N = 150 N

 

So, the correct answer is: 150 N.

 

**An astronaut who weighs 90 kg on Earth will weigh 150 N on the moon**

questions.question: Find the efficiency of a pulley system which has a mechanical advantage of 2.5 and where the load lifts by 2.5 meters on pulling the rope by 10 m.

__**Concept:**__

**Mechanical advantage:**

__
 
• It is a number that tells us how many times a simple machine multiplies the effort force. 
 
• is defined as the **ratio of output force to input force.**
 
• The mechanical advantage of a machine gives its efficiency. 
 
• Formula, MA=(F₀)/(F_i), where, F₀ = output force, Fᵢ = input force
 
• It is a unitless and dimensionless quantity.

**Efficiency:**

 
• The efficiency of a machine is the **ratio of the work done on the load by the machine to the work done on the machine by the effort.**
 
• Thus, it is the ratio of useful work done by the machine output to the work done by the machine input.
 
• It is represented by the Greek symbol η.
 
• Formula, efficiency, eta=(mechanical advantage)/(velocity ratio)

Velocity ratio:

 
• The ratio of the distance moved by the point at which the effort is applied in a simple machine to the distance moved by the point at which the load is applied at the same time.
 
• Formula, velocity ratio=(distance moved by effort)/(distance moved by load)
 
• In the case of an ideal (frictionless and weightless) machine, velocity ratio = mechanical advantage.

**Calculation:**__

Given: mechanical advantage, MA = 2.5, length of load lift, LR = 2.5 m, length of effort, LE = 10 m

Velocity ratio, v=(10)/(2.5)=4

Efficiency, eta=(mechanical advantage)/(velocity ratio)

eta=(2.5)/(4)=0.625

**In percentage, the efficiency is 62.50 %.**

**Calorimetry Principle:**

 
• When two bodies of different temperatures are placed in physical contact with each other, the heat is transferred from the body with a higher temperature to the body with a lower temperature until thermal equilibrium is attained between them.
 
• The body at a higher temperature releases heat while the body at a lower temperature absorbs heat.
 
• **The principle of calorimetry indicates the law of conservation energy,** i.e. the total heat lost by the hot body is equal to the total heat gained by the cold body.
 
• **Heat Lost = Heat Gained**
 
• 
 
**The heat transfer in a system is calculated using the formula, Q = mcΔT**, Where Q = the measure of heat transfer, m = the mass of the body, c = the specific heat of the body, Δt = the change in the temperature

T = 20 ºC

**Hence, the final equilibrium temperature is 20 ºC.**

**MPFI (Multi-point fuel injection) system:**

 
• MPFI (Multi-point fuel injection) system is used with a carburetor, assuring proper air-fuel ratio to the engine by electrically injecting fuel in accordance with various driving conditions.
 
• MPFI system injects fuel into individual cylinders, based on commands from the 'onboard engine management system computer' - popularly known as the engine control unit/ECU.
 
• These techniques result in better 'power balance' amongst the cylinders, higher output from each of them, and faster throttle response.
 
• The electronic fuel injection system supplies the combustion chambers with an air/fuel mixture of optimized ratio under widely varying driving conditions.
 
• **The sensor used in the MPFI system senses the information in the form of physical and chemical variables and sends it to the engine control unit/ECU.**
 
• Sensors are essential components of automotive electronic control systems.
 
• **Sensors are defined as "devices that transform or transduce physical quantities such as mass, pressure, volume, temperature, or acceleration (called measurands) into output signals (usually electrical) that serve as inputs for control systems.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b442a8dfaf632f7af8b8002c7262b28d740fb6f3a6d97d0149f116834417fd5c.png]

• Air intake system
 
• Fuel delivery system
 
• Electronic control system

**Air intake system:**

 
• The air (corresponding to the throttle valve opening) is filtered by the air cleaner, passes through the throttle body, is distributed by the intake manifold, and is finally drawn into each combustion chamber.
 
• When the IAC (intake air control) valve is opened according to the signal from ECM, the air bypasses the throttle valve through a bypass passage and is finally drawn into the intake manifold.

**Fuel delivery system:**

 
• The fuel in the fuel tank is pumped up by the fuel under pressure to each injector through the delivery pipe.
 
• As the fuel pressure applied to the injector is always kept a certain amount higher than the pressure in the intake manifold by the fuel pressure regulator, the fuel is injected into the intake port of the cylinder head when the injector opens according to the injection signal from ECM.
 
• The fuel relieved by the fuel pressure regulator return through the fuel return to the fuel tank.

**Electronic control system:**

 
• The electronic control system consists of various sensors which detect the state of the engine and driving conditions, ECM controls various devices according to the signals from the sensors and various controlled devices.
 
• The systems are:
 
 
• Fuel injection control system
 
• Idle speed control system
 
• Fuel pump control system
 
• Ignition control system
 
• Radiator fan control system.

• In sheet metal work, different types of metal sheets are used. The sheets are specified by standard gauge numbers.

• The cheapest sheet metal is black iron, which is rolled to the desired thickness.

• The use of this metal is limited to articles that are to be painted or enameled such as tanks, fans, stoves, pipes, etc.

• Zinc-coated iron is known as ‘galvanized iron.
 
• This soft iron sheet is popularly known as the GI sheet.
 
• The zinc coating resists rust, improves the appearance of the metal, and permits it to be soldered with greater ease.
 
• Because it is coated with zinc, galvanized sheet iron withstands contact with water and exposure to weather.
 
• Articles such as fans, buckets, furnaces, heating ducts, cabinets, gutters, etc. are made mainly from GI sheets.

• This is an alloy of steel with nickel, chromium, and other metals.

• Gutters, expansion joints, roof flashings, hoods, utensils, and boiler plates are some of the common examples where the copper sheet is used.

• This is used for nearly all solder work, as it is the easiest metal to join by soldering.

questions.question: Which of the following is a temporary joint?
questions.solution:
**Explanation:**

**Press fit joint:**

 
• A press fit, also known as an interference fit, is the fastening of two parts that is achieved by normal force, friction, and cold welding.
 
• **It is a temporary joint.**
 
• This happens when a shaft is inserted tightly into a slightly smaller hole in another part, with the interference holding both parts in place.
 
• It is a form of fastening between two tight-fitting mating parts that produce a joint that is held together by friction after the parts are pushed together.
 
• Depending on the amount of interference, parts may be joined using a tap from a hammer or pressed together using a hydraulic ram.
 
• Critical components that must not sustain damage during joining may also be cooled significantly below room temperature to shrink one of the components before fitting.
 
• This method allows the components to be joined without force and produce a shrink-fit interference when the component returns to normal temperature.

**Welding:**

 
• Welding is a fabrication process that joins materials, usually metals or thermoplastics, by using high heat to melt the parts together and allowing them to cool, causing fusion.
 
• **It is a permanent joint.**
 
• Welding is distinct from lower temperature techniques such as brazing and soldering, which do not melt the base metal (parent metal).
 
• In addition to melting the base metal, a filler material is typically added to the joint to form a pool of molten material (the weld pool) that cools to form a joint that, based on weld configuration (butt, full penetration, fillet, etc.), can be stronger than the base material.
 
• Pressure may also be used in conjunction with heat or by itself to produce a weld.
 
• Welding also requires a form of shield to protect the filler metals or melted metals from being contaminated or oxidized.
 
• Many different energy sources can be used for welding, including a gas flame (chemical), an electric arc (electrical), a laser, an electron beam, friction, and ultrasound. 

**Riveting:**

 
• Riveting is one of the methods of making **permanent joints** of two or more pieces (Metal strips).
 
• It is customary to use rivets of the same metal as that of the parts that are being joined together.
 
• Rivets are used for joining metal sheets and plates in fabrication work, such as bridges, shipbuilding, games, and structural steelwork.

**Soldering:**

 
• Soldering is a process in which two or more items are joined by melting and putting a filler metal (solder) into the joint, the filler metal having a lower melting point than the adjoining metal.
 
• **It is a permanent joint.**
 
• Unlike welding, soldering does not involve melting the work pieces.

Constructional features of inline type F.I.P:

 
• When the plunger is at its bottom position fuel enters through the barrel’s inlet port from the feed pump, fills the space above the plunger in the barrel and excess fuel flows out through the spill port.
 
• In a primed system, the barrel, all the pipes, and the entire system are filled with fuel.
 
• As the plunger rises up due to cam operation, a certain amount of fuel is pushed out of the barrel through the ports.
 
• As soon as the ports are closed by the plunger, the flow of fuel is stopped and the fuel above the plunger in the barrel is trapped and pressurized.
 
• The pressure increases to as high as 400 to 700 bar (kgf / cm²).
 
• This pressure lifts the fuel delivery valve and the fuel enters the fuel line which is connected to the injector.
 
• As the pipe is already full of fuel the extra fuel that is being pumped causes a rise in the pressure throughout the line and lifts the injector valve.
 
• This permits the fuel to be sprayed into the combustion chamber in a fine mist form.
 
• It continues until the lower edge of the helical groove in the plunger uncovers the port in the barrel.
 
• As soon as the port is uncovered, the fuel passes downwards through the vertical slot and flows to the port.
 
• This causes a drop in pressure and the delivery valve closes under the pressure of its spring.
 
• With the consequent drop in the fuel line the injector valve also closes and cuts off the fuel injection.
 
• The plunger stroke is always constant.
 
• But by rotation of the plunger in the barrel, it is possible to deliver the fuel earlier or later in the stroke and control the quantity of fuel sprayed.
 
• The rotation of the plunger is obtained by operating the control rack, which is in turn connected to the governor.

questions.question: Which of the following (gears) converts rotary motion into linear motion?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Rack and pinion:**

 
• Rack and pinion gears are utilized to convert rotation into linear motion.
 
• The flat, toothed component is known as the rack, and the gear is known as the pinion.
 
• A rack and pinion gear system is made up of two gears.
 
• The pinion gear is a conventional round gear, and the rack can be straight or flat.
 
• The pinion gear's teeth mesh with the teeth cut into the rack.
 
• A rack and pinion linear actuator is made up of a circular gear (the pinion) that engages with a linear gear (the rack).
 
• **Together, they transform rotational motion into linear motion and vice versa.**
 
• The rack is driven in a straight path when the pinion is rotated.
 
• Moving the rack linearly, on the other hand, causes the pinion to revolve.
 
• Straight and helical gears can be used in a rack and pinion drive.

• In a helical gear, the teeth are cut at an angle to the axis of rotation.
 
• It is used to transmit power between two parallel shafts.
 
• The end thrust is exerted by the driving and driven gears in the case of helical gears and the thrust may be eliminated by using double helical gears.
 
• These gears are called herringbone gears.

• This system transmits motion at right angles to the axis of motion at different planes.

__**Explanation:**__

**Heat treatment:**

 
• The properties of metal depend upon its composition and its structure.
 
• These properties can be changed to a considerable extent, by changing either their composition or their structure.
 
• The structure of metal can be changed by heating it to a particular temperature, and then, allowing it to cool at a definite rate.
 
• The process of changing the structure and thus changing the properties of metal, by heating and cooling, is called ‘heat treatment of steel’.

**Various heat treatment processes:**

**Annealing:**

 
• Annealing consists of heating a metal to a specific temperature based on the carbon content, holding it at that temperature for a set length of time, and then cooling it very slowly in the furnace

**Full annealing is used to obtain the following properties:**

 
• To relieve the internal stresses and strains developed by various fabrication methods like forgings, castings, etc.
 
• To improve properties of elasticity and ductility.
 
• To reduce hardness.

**Normalizing:**

 
• Normalizing is a type of heat treatment applicable to ferrous metals only.
 
• It differs from annealing in that the metal is heated to a higher temperature and then remove from the furnace for air cooling.

**Normalizing may be employed to:**

 
• To remove the internal stresses induced by heat treating, welding, casting, forging, forming, or machining.
 
• Refine the grain and provide a homogeneous microstructure, to improve response to hardening treatment.
 
• Improve machining characteristics.

**Tempering:**

 
• Tempering consists of heating the steel to a specific temperature generally below its hardening temperature, holding it at that temperature for the required length of time, and then cooling it, usually in still air.

**Purpose of Tempering:**

 
• Steels in its hardened condition, it is often harder than necessary, generally too brittle, and too severally strained in the quenching operation.
 
• The aim of tempering is:
 
 
• To relieve the steel from internal stresses and strains.
 
• To regulate the hardness and toughness
 
• To decrease the brittleness and restore some ductility to induce shock resistance.

Valves of Engine:

Functions of valves:

 
• To open and close the inlet and exhaust passages of the cylinder.
 
• To dissipate heat, through its seat to the cylinder head.

Construction of a valve:

 
• The head (1) of the valve is ground with a margin (2) to provide strength.
 
• The valve face (3) is ground to a 30° or 45° angle which matches with the seat angle to avoid leakage.
 
• The valve stem (4) is of round shape.
 
• The length of the stem varies from engine to engine.
 
• At the end of the stem a groove (5) is provided to hold the spring lock.
 
• **Valve spring remover is used to remove and refit valves in a cylinder head.**
 
• In some heavy-duty engines, the valves are hollow, and sodium is filled inside, which helps in the quick cooling of the valve.

Valve Materials:

 
• Inlet valve: Nickel-chromium steel alloy with stellite facing
 
• Exhaust valve: Silicon-chrome alloy steel sodium-filled valves
